newsitem.title: USA: Feds to examine $500,000 gift to Democrats - report.
newsitem.headline: Feds to examine $500,000 gift to Democrats - report.

text.p: A federal probe into fund-raising activities of a former White House deputy chief of staff will examine a $500,000 gift to the Democrats, the largest single donation to the party last year, the Boston Globe reported Friday.
Arnold Hiatt of Weston, Mass. gave $500,000 to the party last year after discussing how to make the donation with deputy Chief of Staff Harold Ickes, the newspaper reported.

"We will be looking at it," said Michael Lawrence, a spokesman for the independent Office of the Special Counsel, which is in charge of investigating whether federal officials violated campaign solicitation laws.
Arnold, the former chairman of athletic footwear maker Stride Rite Corp., made the donation last fall.
Lawrence told the Globe the probe focused only on whether Ickes violated the law barring federal officials from soliciting campaign funds.
